proposed.explanation:
COMI (Commercial International Bank of Egypt) shows strong fundamental growth in FY2025 versus FY2024: net loans grew ~48% (from 343.5 bn to 508.0 bn EGP), customer deposits grew ~14% (from 972.6 bn to 1,110.4 bn EGP), net interest income grew ~18% (from 91.1 bn to 107.7 bn EGP), and basic EPS rose ~24% (from 14.72 to 18.25 EGP per share). At the current price of 128 EGP, the implied P/E is roughly 7×, which is low for a bank posting this rate of earnings growth. For an investor seeking high growth over a 10-year horizon with high loss tolerance and no liquidity needs, this profile is attractive.

However, the evidence is limited: we have only one year of comparison, no data on asset quality (NPLs, provisions), capital adequacy, total revenue, net profit, ROE, or dividend policy. The very high 48% loan growth, while positive, could also signal aggressive credit expansion that may later require provisioning. These gaps mean the decision carries meaningful uncertainty.

The diversification rule caps any single holding at 50% of total portfolio value. With 15,000 EGP cash and a price of 128 EGP, the maximum number of COMI shares that keeps the position at or below 50% is 58 shares (58 × 128 = 7,424 EGP; 7,424 / 15,000 ≈ 49.5%). I recommend buying 58 shares, leaving 7,576 EGP in cash to preserve diversification headroom for future additions. This is guidance, not a guarantee; the limited evidence base and the absence of asset-quality and capital-adequacy data are material risks.
